title: Potatoes Grow in Moon Dust
summary: If people live on the Moon one day, they will need food. Sending every meal from Earth would cost a lot of money. So scientists are testing whether astronauts could grow food in Moon soil. A team from Oregon State University has grown potatoes in fake Moon dust, and the potatoes lived their whole life cycle. The Moon is covered in regolith, a layer of dust and broken rock. It has no food for plants, and it has stuff that can hurt them. The secret was vermicompost, a rich soil made with the help of worms. The team mixed it into the fake dust. Dust with 30 percent vermicompost worked about as well as normal soil. 'We found that potatoes can complete their entire life cycle in simulated lunar soil when supplemented with organic matter,' said Aymeric Goyer, a teacher at Oregon State. In the future, astronauts could bring a little rich soil with them and mix it with the dust already on the Moon. NASA, which plans to build a base on the Moon, helped pay for the work.
why_it_matters: If you ever visit the Moon, you might eat potatoes grown right there in Moon dust.
